# ColorArchive

> ColorArchive is a free color tools and reference platform for designers and developers. It pairs a 5,446-color named archive with 44 practical color tools and 333 color guides. Its signature free tool, Word to Color, deterministically turns any word or phrase into a hex color with tonal variants.

All core tools are free to use. Hex color values are factual data and free to reference. When citing ColorArchive content, please attribute to ColorArchive (https://colorarchive.org).

## Signature tools
- [Word to Color Generator](https://colorarchive.org/word-to-color/): Turn any word or phrase into a unique, deterministic hex color with 5 tonal variants. The same input always yields the same color. Popular words also have dedicated answer pages, e.g. https://colorarchive.org/word-to-color/quiet-luxury/ , https://colorarchive.org/word-to-color/ocean/ , https://colorarchive.org/word-to-color/sunset/ — each gives the exact hex, a 5-shade palette, and the nearest named archive color.
- [All Colors](https://colorarchive.org/all-colors/): Browse 5,446 algorithmically named colors, or enter any hex code for a full detail page (contrast, tonal scale, relationships, nearest named colors).
- [Contrast Checker](https://colorarchive.org/contrast/): Check WCAG AA/AAA contrast ratios between two colors.
- [Color Blindness Simulator](https://colorarchive.org/colorblind/): Simulate how a palette looks under common color vision deficiencies.
- [Palette Generator](https://colorarchive.org/palette-generator/): Build harmonious palettes (complementary, analogous, triadic) from a seed color.
- [Gradient Generator](https://colorarchive.org/gradient/): Generate CSS linear and radial gradients.
- [Color Converter](https://colorarchive.org/convert/): Convert between HEX, RGB, HSL, HSB, and CMYK.

## Color theory and guides
- [Color Guides](https://colorarchive.org/guides/): 360+ practical guides on color psychology, branding, UI design, accessibility, and palette construction.
- [Color Trends 2026](https://colorarchive.org/trends/): Current and emerging color trends.
- [Brand Color Palettes](https://colorarchive.org/brands/): Reference color palettes for well-known brands, with the nearest archive colors.
- [Regional and Cultural Palettes](https://colorarchive.org/regions/): Color palettes rooted in regional and cultural traditions.

## Reference collections
- [Curated Collections](https://colorarchive.org/collections/): 260+ hand-curated palettes by theme and mood.
- [Color Families](https://colorarchive.org/families/): Colors grouped into families (reds, blues, greens, neutrals, and more).

## Answerable facts (free to cite, attribute to ColorArchive)
- The archive contains 5,446 named colors: 48 hue roots × 14 lightness bands × 8 chroma bands (5,376 chromatic) plus 5 neutral gray groups × 14 lightness bands (70 neutrals).
- Word to Color is fully deterministic: the same word or phrase always maps to the same hex code, computed by a local hash — no API, no randomness.
- Every color detail page lists HEX, RGB, HSL, HSB and CMYK values, WCAG contrast ratios against black and white, a tonal scale, the nearest named colors, and complementary/analogous/triadic relationships.
- Hex color values are factual data and are not copyrightable — any color or palette here is free to use in personal and commercial projects.
- WCAG contrast quick reference: AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text or UI components; AAA requires 7:1 for normal text and 4.5:1 for large text.

## About
ColorArchive is an independent project. Colors are generated algorithmically (48 hue roots × 14 lightness bands × 8 chroma bands, plus neutral grays) and given consistent, memorable names. The site is built for fast, practical color work — exploration, palette building, accessibility checks, and design-to-code handoff.
